title: GDC: Integration of Multi-Omic and Phenotypic Resources to Unravel the Genetic Pathogenesis of Hearing Loss.
authors: Cheng, Hui; Wang, Xuegang; Zhong, Mingjun; Geng, Jia; Li, Wenjian; Pei, Kanglu; Wang, Jing; Wang, Lanchen; Lu, Yu; Cheng, Jing; Bu, Fengxiao; Yuan, Huijun
one_liner_zh: 该文构建耳聋遗传数据库并整合多组学数据，虽涉及转录因子DNA结合域突变热点和候选基因预测，但核心是数据资源整合与表型关联，非TF-DNA互作机制建模，方法上仅用SMOTE-Random Forest，与课题聚焦的AI/物理模拟结合建模关联有限。
abstract: Effective research and clinical application in audiology and hearing loss (HL) require the integration of diverse data, yet the absence of a dedicated database impedes understanding and insight extraction in HL. To address this, the Genetic Deafness Commons (GDC) is developed by consolidating extensive genetic and genomic data from 51 public databases and the Chinese Deafness Genetics Consortium. This repository comprises 5 983 613 variants across 201 HL genes, revealing the genetic landscape of HL and identifying six novel mutational hotspots within the DNA-binding domains of transcription factors. Comparative phenotypic analyses highlighted considerable disparities between human and mouse models. Among the 201 human HL genes, 133 exhibit hearing abnormalities in mice; 35 have been tested in mice without exhibiting a hearing loss phenotype; and 33 lack auditory testing data. Moreover, gene expression analyses in the cochleae of mice, humans, and rhesus macaques demonstrated a notable correlation (R(2) 0.718-0.752). Utilizing gene expression, function, pathway, and phenotype data, a SMOTE-Random Forest model identified 18 candidate HL genes, including TBX2, newly confirmed as an HL gene. As a comprehensive and unified repository, the GDC advances audiology research and practice by improving data accessibility and usability, ultimately fostering deeper insights into hearing disorders.
abstract_zh: 听力学和听力损失（HL）的有效研究与临床应用需要整合多样化的数据，然而缺乏专用数据库阻碍了对HL的理解和洞察提取。为解决这一问题，通过整合来自51个公共数据库和中国耳聋遗传学联盟的大量遗传与基因组数据，开发了遗传性耳聋共享库（GDC）。该资源库包含201个HL基因中的5 983 613个变异，揭示了HL的遗传图谱，并识别出转录因子DNA结合域内的六个新型突变热点。比较表型分析强调了人类和小鼠模型之间的显著差异。在201个人类HL基因中，133个在小鼠中表现出听觉异常；35个已在小鼠中测试但未显示听力损失表型；33个缺乏听觉测试数据。此外，小鼠、人类和恒河猴耳蜗中的基因表达分析显示出显著相关性（R(2) 0.718-0.752）。利用基因表达、功能、通路和表型数据，SMOTE-随机森林模型识别出18个候选HL基因，其中包括新确认为HL基因的TBX2。作为一个全面且统一的资源库，GDC通过提高数据可访问性和可用性推进听力学研究与实践，最终促进对听力障碍的更深入理解。
